problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a circuit of maintenance checks at seven key facilities across a region.  
The facilities are positioned at the following grid coordinates:  

Facility Alpha: (107,197)  
Facility Beta: (169,181)  
Facility Gamma: (11,42)  
Facility Delta: (114,16)  
Facility Epsilon: (66,179)  
Facility Zeta: (40,114)  
Facility Theta: (135,124)  

Travel distances between facilities, expressed in kilometers, are predetermined:  

Alpha to Gamma: 182.3 km  
Alpha to Delta: 181.1 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 44.8 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 106.7 km  
Alpha to Theta: 78.2 km  
Beta to Gamma: 210.4 km  
Beta to Delta: 173.9 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 103.0 km  
Beta to Zeta: 145.4 km  
Beta to Theta: 66.4 km  
Gamma to Delta: 106.2 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 147.6 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 77.6 km  
Gamma to Theta: 148.7 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 169.9 km  
Delta to Zeta: 122.8 km  
Delta to Theta: 110.0 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 70.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 88.2 km  
Zeta to Theta: 95.5 km  

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct route exists between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta.  
Moreover, owing to scheduling restrictions, exactly one of the two following connections must be part of the inspection circuit: the route between Beta and Gamma, or the route between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed tour that visits each facility precisely once and returns to the origin facility.
